## Exact result

A proof candidate for OWR2008/44, Conjecture4 (problem30001075): the union of common tangent lines to any three pairwise disjoint convex subsets of R3 is contained in a Lebesgue-null set. This includes nonclosed, unbounded, and lower-dimensional sets. Tangency uses the source's supporting-plane definition.

## Proof and review

- CANDIDATE.md contains the complete cap-chart / density-point / area-formula proof
- A separate adversarial reviewer found no remaining mathematical gap in the complete scope, at SHA256 b04aaf0b5a42d79ad26daf27880774a3f126858ef545b3f366a2b8b62e277252
- Four unchanged independent review/check artifacts are included under review/
- Local exact checks: 810 support-function increments, 4 cap-margin models, 81 illustrative contraction systems, and symbolic Jacobian / Vandermonde / planar-contact identities
- Independent exact diagnostics: 36 passed

Historical priority remains unconfirmed. AI review is not external peer review. The stronger countable-union-of-2-manifolds conjecture is not claimed.

The candidate remains byte-identical to the reviewed version; its historical pre-review header is explained by README.md. Source and limited novelty checks are recorded in LITERATURE.md. No source PDFs are redistributed.

The campaign parent owns the single QUEUE row update to claimed_solved; this worker's commit changes only attempts/30001075. No merge or release is requested.
title: Research 30001075: reviewed common-tangent measure-zero proof
